image_description: A low-angle shot of a traffic light assembly against an overcast sky. The primary subject is a vertical traffic signal head showing red, amber, and green lights illuminated simultaneously (or appearing so due to exposure/long shutter). It is mounted on a horizontal mast arm attached to a vertical pole. There are additional street light fixtures and silhouetted trees in the background.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The rectangular object at the top right (possibly a sign or another light back) has warped geometry and unclear connection points, appearing slightly melted into the sky.

All three lights (Red, Amber, Green) appear illuminated simultaneously with equal intensity. While possible in long-exposure photography, in AI generation this often indicates a failure to understand the mutual exclusivity of traffic states, resulting in a 'glowing' artifact rather than distinct state lighting.
The connection between the horizontal mast arm and the vertical pole is somewhat vague and lacks clear mechanical detail (bolts/brackets), appearing slightly fused.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific class identity and rule out misclassification as generic street lamps.
To verify the physical connectivity of the cantilevered arm and ensure no floating elements in the background.
To check for edge bleeding between the black housing and the gray sky, and ensure visors are solidly attached.
To assess the realism of the simultaneous lighting artifact and general noise/grain consistency.

focus_areas: Mechanical integrity of the mast arm attachment
Realism of the simultaneous red/amber/green illumination
Boundary sharpness of the signal housing against the sky
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'simultaneous lighting' of the traffic signals. Determine if this is a plausible photographic artifact (long exposure) or an AI semantic error. Scrutinize the background objects for geometric warping.
